The hands-on hour. Make a volcano plot you'd be proud to put in a paper.
**Use your AI assistant freely.** One possible solution is on the website — try first!

## Setup — run this first

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(ggrepel)
data_dir <- if (dir.exists("data")) "data" else if (dir.exists("../data")) "../data" else "project/data"
de <- read_tsv(file.path(data_dir, "DE_biofilm_vs_planktonic_24h.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE)

de_plot <- de %>%
  mutate(
    padj = ifelse(padj == 0, min(padj[padj > 0], na.rm = TRUE), padj),
    status = case_when(
      padj < 0.05 & log2FoldChange >  1 ~ "Up in biofilm",
      padj < 0.05 & log2FoldChange < -1 ~ "Down in biofilm",
      TRUE                              ~ "Not significant"
    )
  )
```

## Your mission

Build a polished volcano from `de_plot` that:

1. shows dashed threshold lines (fold change ±1, p = 0.05);
2. **labels the ~10 most significant genes** (hint: `ggrepel::geom_text_repel`);
3. has a clean theme, a clear title, and colourblind-friendly colours;
4. you can explain to a colleague in one sentence.

> 🤖 **Ask your AI:** *"How do I label only the top 10 genes on a ggplot volcano with
> ggrepel?"* · *"Suggest a colourblind-friendly palette for up/down/ns."* — then **run it,
> read it, and check it.**
